body:
### Has anyone run DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (2.25-bit) on 1× V100 32GB?

I’m considering running **DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 2.25-bit (IQ2_XS)** with Strata or Project Maya on this setup:

- **GPU:** 1× Tesla V100 32GB (PCIe 3.0)
- **CPU:** Intel Xeon E5-2697 v4
- **RAM:** 64GB DDR4-2133 ECC (8×8GB)
- **Storage:** 2TB NVMe, with >1TB free
- **OS/stack:** Linux, CUDA 12-compatible driver

Has anyone tried a similar V100 setup? I’m mainly wondering:

1. What tokens/sec did you get?
2. Did you use the 4-bit MXFP4 KV cache, and how much VRAM did it use?
3. Any V100-specific flags or issues with Strata/Maya?

Answering from the 3x V100 32 GB + 128 GB DDR3L rig this benchmark is from. We have not run 2.25-bit on a single V100, but the capacity math plus our off-GPU traffic costs bracket what to expect.

**Capacity first.** The 2.25-bit (IQ2_XS) set is ~274 GB with the Engram the setup adds; the 2.00bpw set we ran was 232 GiB (129 GiB of weights + 103 GiB Engram). Your 32 GB VRAM + 64 GB RAM is ~96 GB, so roughly two thirds of the expert traffic would be served from the NVMe. For calibration: our rig (3x 32 GB = 96 GB VRAM, 128 GB RAM) kept ~91 % of expert traffic resident and still decoded at only 17-22 tok/s (Strata, numbers in this issue's body); the off-GPU expert fetch cost we measured on our DDR3L box is ~9-12 ms per expert group. At ~2/3 of the traffic off-GPU, a single V100 lands in the single-digit tok/s band. It will run; it will not be a daily driver.

**The cheapest transformation is RAM, not GPU.** The E5-2697 v4 platform takes cheap DDR4-2133 ECC; at 128-256 GB most experts leave the NVMe entirely and you are in the band we measured, with one card instead of three doing the compute (expect the low end of it).

On your specific questions:

1. Three-card numbers are in the issue body (17.4 / 22.0 tok/s medium/long, engine-measured, prefill 176, correctness probes passed). Single card: not measured — the extrapolation above.
2. We ran the default KV at the default 8K context and did not test the 4-bit MXFP4 KV cache, so no VRAM figure for it; worth checking whether the engine even offers it on sm_70 — Volta has no native MXFP4 path.
3. V100 specifics we hit: CUDA 12.x only (13 drops Volta); on Strata, sm_70 needs a source build with `STRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60` (recipe in this issue); `--ple-io ram` only matters if the PLE table lands on a spinning disk — on NVMe the default is fine; the Windows commit-limit/pagefile trap we documented elsewhere does not apply to Linux.

If the goal is DeepSeek-class quality on exactly one V100 + 64 GB today, the 2.25-bit set is the wrong size — either budget the RAM, or run one of the Qwen tiers that actually fit resident.

Thank you for measuring this and writing it up. We are building a Strata website with a page for community benchmarks, and results like these will be added there when it launches, so we are closing this here. If your numbers change with a new version, you are welcome to post them again.
